agenda_briefs.title: Council to hear floodplain resilience delegation from Lower Fraser Floodplains Coalition
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will receive a delegation from the Lower Fraser Floodplains Coalition, presented by Habitat Program Director Lina Azeez, seeking the City's sign-on to a regional Joint Statement for Action on Floodplain Resilience in the Lower Mainland. The Metro Vancouver Regional District Board endorsed the Joint Statement on May 29, 2026, following review by its Air Quality Committee. The statement calls on local governments and First Nations to jointly advocate for stable, long-term federal and provincial investment in flood resilience. No decision has been made and no bylaw or policy change has been approved.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council decision — new floodplain rules could affect development or building permits on your property.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider Urban Forest Strategy 2026 status update
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will receive a status update on the first year of its Urban Forest Strategy, adopted May 2025, which targets raising tree canopy cover from 32% (2022) to 40% by 2075. Staff report progress on governance, tree data, natural asset management and policy work. Key for property owners and developers: the Tree Bylaw and Tree Management Policy updates, plus a new Tree Reserve Fund, are scheduled for early 2027, and Zoning Bylaw changes adding minimum tree cover and permeable ground requirements are set for 2026. Tree replacement fees were already updated.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the Zoning Bylaw update in 2026 and the Tree Bylaw rewrite in early 2027, which will change tree-protection and tree-cover requirements for development and property.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider free mulch and compost program request
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is set to consider correspondence from resident Tessy Chalissery urging the city to create a plan for food self-sufficiency, including a free mulch and compost pickup program like Port Coquitlam's annual one-week event, and allowing small-scale backyard chicken coops of four to five egg-laying hens as Surrey permits. The item was referred from the Community Consultation Panel meeting of September 22, 2026. No decision has been made; council could direct staff to investigate, refer it to a committee, or take no action.
